close_reason: Superseded by decision (Mark, 2026-05-12, attended session): rescope per Option (A). PKITS-through-wrappers structurally infeasible (PKITS EE certs lack SAN and EKU). Replaced by PKIX-fmtv.22 (curated TLS hostname corpus + verify_tls_server tests) and PKIX-fmtv.23 (curated mailbox corpus + verify_smime_*  tests). verify_chain PKITS coverage stays where it already is (pkix-chain/tests/e2e.rs e2e_verify_chain_default_pkits_4_1_1 + pkix-difftest pkix_path oracle). Code-signing/timestamping wrappers covered by targeted unit tests, no curated corpus needed (no identity-string target). See decision rationale in superseding beads' descriptions.
description:
**Rescoped 2026-05-11 after code-state audit.**

Original framing (PKITS through verify()) is partially done: `pkix-chain/tests/e2e.rs:42` (`e2e_verify_chain_default_pkits_4_1_1`) already exercises `verify_chain_default` against a PKITS chain. `pkix-difftest`'s pkix_path oracle (`pkix-difftest/src/oracles/pkix_path.rs:107`) runs `validate_path` against the full PKITS corpus.

What remains: **PKITS regression for the NEW per-use wrappers** (verify_tls_server, verify_smime_signer, verify_code_signer, etc.) once they ship.

For each new wrapper:
- Identify PKITS test cases applicable to its use case (e.g., the EE certs in PKITS §4.1 have `id-kp-clientAuth` EKU; some §4.x tests use `id-kp-emailProtection`).
- Run the wrapper against the PKITS bundle for each applicable test.
- Confirm outcome matches PKITS expected verdict.
- Hostname/mailbox binding test cases (RFC 6125 §6.4 wildcards, RFC 8398 internationalized mailbox) — PKITS does not exercise these; add separate curated test corpus.

Acceptance: per-wrapper pass-rate documented in `pkix-difftest/baseline-pkits-wrappers.md`.

**Blocks on:** `.15` (ergonomic wrappers must ship before they can be PKITS-tested).
title: PKITS regression through new verify_* wrappers
